question: Starting at 12 m/s, a scooter holds 1.2 m/s^2 for 10 s down a test straight. The examiner's last box on the sheet is the final velocity.
The rocket sled enters the arrestor at 50 m/s. Deceleration is -12 m/s^2 and the burn lasts 4 s; what speed remains when it stops firing? The rails run for 300 m.
A delivery van was already rolling. Through the timed gate it goes in at 16 m/s and gains 2.5 m/s^2 for the 6 s the clock runs; what does the speed read as it leaves?
v0 = 9 m/s, a = 3 m/s^2, t = 15 s, find v.
A parachutist steps out of a hovering balloon and thereafter speeds up by 4.9 metres per second every second; 5 s on, how fast is she falling?
Take a rollerblader coasting at 2.5 m/s, add 8 m/s^2 for 4 s, and state the speed at the end.
A landing aircraft rolls onto the runway at 35 m/s; with a = -9.5 m/s^2 the brakes hold for 3 s before it turns off, so the airspeed indicator shows what?
A forklift is doing 24 m/s when the load shifts and it slows at -5 m/s^2. The aisle runs 30 m and the truck is 2 s into the skid, so what speed is left?
Run 4 in the logbook: entry speed 6 m/s, acceleration 6 m/s^2, duration 7 s. What speed closes the row?
How fast is the train still going? It was doing 45 m/s when the brakes went on at -7 m/s^2, and 3 s later the driver lifts off.
A lift cable snaps at 75 m and the car drops in free fall; taking g = 9.8 m/s^2, and ignoring the guide rails and any air, find the speed the car has at the pit floor.
With g = 9.81 m/s^2, what speed does a pebble released from 2 m reach just before it touches down?
A diver in training steps off a 4.5 m board. Ignoring air resistance and taking g = 9.8 m/s^2, the figure the coach is waiting for is her entry speed.
The drop rig holds its weight 30 m up and lets go. With g = 9.8 m/s^2, what speed does the contact pad print?
A stone leaves the lip of a 60 m cliff and falls freely. With 9.8 metres per second squared as gravity, how fast is it going at the bottom?
A lifeguard drops a buoy 20 m from a gantry over the water; the gantry stands 3 m back from the edge. With g = 9.81 m/s^2, what speed does the buoy reach the surface at?
How fast is a dropped toolbox moving at the ground? It leaves a 15 m scaffold and g there is 9.81 m/s^2.
A spanner slips off a ledge 6.4 m up, and a bystander says it hits at more than 15 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s^2 and check that.
A ball bearing is let go 0.5 m above a sensor plate. The plate logs the speed at contact, and g = 10 m/s^2, so what does it log?
h = 1.2 m, g = 10 m/s^2, release from rest. Impact speed?
An 18 kg parcel rides the conveyor at 5 m/s. What momentum does it hold?
Two players warm up on the field. One, a 7 kg medicine ball, is thrown downfield at 14 m/s, and the coach asks for the momentum.
At 2 m/s a trolley carrying 45 kg of cement rolls across the yard. How much momentum is in that motion?
The launcher fires a 0.25 kg slug and the chronograph shows 24 m/s; what momentum does the slug leave with?
m = 75 kg, v = 6 m/s. p = ?
A 3 kg shot is released at 9 m/s. It was swung for 2 s on a 1.5 m wire, so how much momentum leaves the hand?
A golf ball of 0.06 kg is struck and leaves the tee at 55 metres per second; how much momentum does it carry away?
What momentum does a loaded van have? It weighs 1500 kg and the dash shows 18 m/s.
A bobsleigh of 850 kg is clocked at 12 m/s and the crew says that is under 10 000 kg m/s. Is the momentum figure they quote right?
A hockey puck leaves the stick and skips down the ice. Its mass is 0.4 kg, it is measured at 32 m/s crossing the blue line, and the stat sheet wants the momentum.
F = 18 N, t = 4 s. Impulse?
Over 60 s a 5 N thrust acts on the satellite. Give the impulse.
A steady 90 N is applied to the handle for 1.2 s, and the question at the end of the practical is the impulse delivered.
A jack pushes with 250 newtons for 2 seconds; what impulse does it pass on?
How much impulse goes into the nail? The hammer delivers 600 N for 0.03 s.
A blocker's hands are on the volleyball for 0.5 s while the force averages 25 N. The stat sheet wants the impulse.
Punch data: 320 N applied for 0.15 s. Impulse, please.
A goalkeeper holds 120 N against the ball for 0.8 s. A coach claims the impulse is under 90 N s; work it out and say if she is right.
Forces are logged by the plate under the runner. It records a steady 40 N for 3.5 s, so what impulse does the runner take?
A 7 N toy motor runs for 12 s and the car travels 4 m. What impulse does the motor give the car?
On the test rig a 55 kg crash dummy is accelerated from 12 m/s to 18 m/s. The load cell integrates the net work, so what does it read?
A 900 kg dragster climbs from 5 metres per second to 25 metres per second over the run; how much net work goes in?
A 6 kg weight goes from 4 m/s to 8 m/s and the trainer says the net work is more than 150 J. Check the number.
A sledge is shoved along the ice and its speed rises over a short push. It weighs 4 kg, starts the push at 2 m/s and is doing 10 m/s when the pusher lets go; the work the pusher did is the answer.
A 10 kg sack quickens, 6 m/s becoming 11 m/s. Net work?
A go-kart of 150 kg is timed at 3 m/s out of the corner and 12 m/s at the end of the straight, so the net work on it over that stretch is what?
v0 = 8 m/s, v = 15 m/s, m = 35 kg. Net work done?
A 0.2 kg dart is fired from a standstill up to 30 m/s. What net work went into it?
A 1.5 kg ball is accelerated from 3 m/s to 7 m/s by a racket that is 68 cm long. What net work was done on the ball?
Starting from rest, take a 0.05 kg bullet and bring it to 400 m/s; the net work required is what?
Moving at 20 m/s under a 450 N thrust, the craft needs what power?
A rower pulls with 60 newtons while the boat keeps 7 metres per second; find the power delivered.
A winch pulls at 900 N and the load rises at 11 m/s, which a hand says is over 9 kW. Check the power.
At what rate is work being done? A 35 N pull moves the crate along at 1.5 m/s.
The treadmill motor reads 12 N of drag while the belt runs at 3 m/s; what power does the motor supply?
An electric scooter holds 80 N of drive force up the incline at a steady 2.5 m/s, and the last question on the sheet asks for the power output.
A 150 N force moves a pallet at 0.5 m/s. The pallet carries 12 boxes. What power is going in?
Take a 1000 N thrust at 40 m/s and give the power.
A tractor drags a plough through a field. The drawbar pull is 500 N and the rig keeps 8 m/s, and the figure the farmer needs is the rate at which work is being done.
A 0.8 kg ball is bowled at 22 metres per second into 3 metres of rough turf, where 45 newtons of friction act; what speed is left?
m = 12 kg, v0 = 9 m/s, friction 15 N, run 6 m, find v.
Take a 9 kg cart doing 12 m/s, put 40 N of friction on it for 2 m, and report the speed it leaves with.
A 3 kg block is timed at 18 m/s entering a 7 m rough patch where friction is 12 N. A lab partner writes that it emerges at under 16 m/s; check that.
A 5 kg puck is already sliding at 14 m/s when it hits the rough end of the rink, where 20 N of friction acts over the last 5 m. The speed as it crosses the line is what the coach wants.
How fast is the sled still going? It starts at 16 m/s, weighs 2.5 kg and loses 30 N to friction over 4 m.
Over 10 m against 20 N of friction, a 7 kg mass that started at 13 m/s ends up at what speed?
The test track records a 40 kg cart entering the friction section at 10 m/s; the brake applies 50 N for the 6 m of the section, and the exit gate prints the speed.
A 1.2 kg ball bearing skims into 5 m of oil, where it meets 60 N of drag having arrived at 30 m/s, and the last thing the apparatus logs is the speed on exit.
A 20 kg crate leaves the ramp at 11 m/s and grinds 8 m over gravel with 25 N of friction. The ramp itself is 4 m tall. Find the speed it keeps.
k = 1200 N/m, x = 0.05 m. Stored energy?
A spring on the launcher is rated 300 N/m and the arm pulls it back 0.12 m before release. The energy the launcher can give the ball is what the test asks for.
Drawn out to 0.45 m, a 90 N/m spring holds how much energy?
Within a 240 N/m spring squashed 0.09 m sits what amount of energy?
A 350 N/m spring is stretched 0.15 m. It hangs from a hook 2 m above the bench. How much energy is tucked away in it?
A 55 N/m spring pulled 0.6 m stores, according to a pupil, more than 12 J. Work it out and say if that is right.
A buffer spring of 450 N/m takes the impact and is driven back 0.16 m, and the quantity the report lists is the elastic energy it absorbed.
A spring of stiffness 180 newtons per metre is squeezed by 0.25 metres; how much energy is held in it?
A 600 N/m spring in the rig is compressed 0.22 m, and the gauge reports the energy stored; what does it report?
Take a 100 N/m spring and extend it by 0.55 m, then give the energy it stores.
How long for one complete swing? The thread runs 1.2 m and g is 9.81 m/s^2.
The clock in the hall has a 3 m rod swinging under g = 9.8 m/s^2; the timing gate reports one period, so what does it report?
L = 2.8 m, g = 10 m/s^2, find T.
A pupil says a 0.7 m pendulum under g = 10 m/s^2 swings slower than once a second. Compute the period and judge the claim.
A pendulum 0.8 metres long is set swinging where gravity is 9.8 metres per second squared; what is its period?
Take a 2.5 m pendulum on a world where g = 10 m/s^2 and give the time of one oscillation.
A thread is only 0.15 m long, the lab's g is 9.8 m/s^2, and the value the worksheet leaves blank is the period of small swings.
Under g = 9.81 m/s^2, what period does a 1.6 m suspension give?
A small brass bob hangs on a thread 0.45 m long in a room where g = 9.8 m/s^2. The stopwatch question is the time for one complete swing.
A 5 m pendulum hangs from a beam 6 m above the floor, with g = 9.81 m/s^2. Find its period.
A 260 N force is applied 0.9 m along a spanner at 80 degrees. The spanner is 12 mm thick. Find the torque.
A 33 N force at 2.2 m and 55 degrees, says a classmate, gives less than 60 N m. Check that.
The torque wrench reads 140 N at 1.1 m from the nut, angled 100 degrees to the handle; the gauge shows the moment, so what does it show?
A crowbar is levered against a crate 0.6 m from the fulcrum. The hand pushes with 200 N at 40 degrees to the bar, and the number the worksheet wants is the turning effect.
What torque does the pivot feel? A 42 N pull is applied 4 m out at 65 degrees to the arm.
A tiny 7 N weight hangs at the end of a 0.5 m arm, the arm being square to the force at 90 degrees, and the last blank on the sheet is the torque.
Take 500 N applied 1.6 m from a pivot at 30 degrees to the arm and state the turning moment.
r = 1.4 m, F = 95 N, theta = 110 degrees. Turning moment?
At 145 degrees to the arm, 6 m from the axis, a 55 N force is applied. Give the torque.
A 16 newton force acts 5 metres from the hinge at 25 degrees to the arm; what turning effect does it produce?
A 750 g bath of water at c = 4.18 J/(g C) is heated by 8 degrees. A plumber says that takes under 20 000 J. Check it.
How much heat does it take to warm a 150 g lead block, c = 0.13 J/(g C), through 80 degrees?
A 200 g can of oil with c = 2.1 J/(g C) rises 24 degrees in a 30 degree room. Find the heat it took in.
A 400 g pane of glass, specific heat 0.84 joule per gram per degree, is warmed by 55 degrees; what energy does that absorb?
Take 1000 g of liquid with c = 4.2 J/(g C), warm it 12 degrees, and report the heat required.
300 g, c = 0.38 J/(g C), 22 degree rise: heat needed?
A 50 g iron weight sits in a bath, c = 0.45 J/(g C), and over the hour its temperature climbs by 48 degrees, so the energy it gained is the last thing to work out.
A 250 g drum of coolant with c = 4.2 J/(g C) is warmed through 45 degrees on the dyno. The heat the radiator has to dump is the figure the engineer needs.
A 100 g silver bar of c = 0.24 J/(g C) goes into the furnace and comes out 65 degrees warmer; the calorimeter logs the heat taken, so what is it?
Through 35 degrees goes a 500 g aluminium casting, c = 0.9 J/(g C). How much heat is absorbed?
A 4 ohm resistor has 5 volts across it; how many amperes pass through it?
A 45 V rail feeds a 9 ohm heater through 2 m of cable. What current does the heater draw?
What current will flow? 7 V is applied across 2 ohms.
The insulation tester puts 100 V across a 20 ohm element and the meter shows the current; what does it show?
Take 27 V and drive it through 3 ohms, then state the current.
A 2.5 V cell across 5 ohms: a pupil claims the current is over 0.6 A. Check the claim.
A coil of 4 ohms is connected to an 8 V source, and the last line of the table asks for the current through it.
Across 7 ohms sits 14 V. Give the current.
V = 60 V, R = 15 ohms. I = ?
A bench supply is set to 30 V and the coil it feeds measures 5 ohms. The ammeter reading is the number the student must record.
A 60 ohm winding carries 0.15 amperes; what potential difference sits across it?
A 30 ohm coil carries 0.4 A from a bench supply. The voltage across the coil is what the table needs.
1.8 A through 12 ohms, a student writes, needs more than 24 V. Check that.
A 7 A current runs in a 6 ohm wire that is 3 m long. What voltage drop appears across it?
What voltage appears? 2.5 A is pushed through 8 ohms.
I = 12 A, R = 5 ohms, V = ?
A 4 ohm load takes 3.5 A, and the value the label leaves blank is the voltage across it.
The shunt reads 0.5 A and the element is 24 ohms; the voltmeter displays what?
Take 0.9 A through 50 ohms and give the voltage.
With 2.5 ohms in the circuit and 20 A flowing, the voltage is what?
Take 1.8 A at 22 V and state the power.
The bench meter shows 3.5 A at 14 V for the lamp; the wattmeter reports what?
At 50 V the device takes 0.4 A. Give the power it uses.
A 36 V supply pushes 0.6 A through a motor that weighs 3 kg. Find the power drawn.
An 18 volt supply drives 2.2 amperes into a heater; at what rate does it deliver energy?
A relay coil holds 12 A at 6 V, and the last box on the form wants the power it dissipates.
0.25 A at 120 V - what do the watts come to?
A small fan on a 6 V supply pulls 1.5 A. The power it consumes is the figure the datasheet lacks.
9 A at 8 V, says a technician, is over 75 W. Check it.
On a 15 m radius, at 45 m/s, the inward acceleration is what?
A toy train takes a 0.5 m curve at 4 m/s, and the last line of the lab report is the centripetal acceleration.
A drone circles a 1.2 m radius on a tether at 9 m/s. The acceleration pointing at the centre is what the operator wants.
At 33 m/s on an 11 m radius a rider claims the acceleration is over 100 m/s^2. Check it.
An object keeps 14 metres per second around a circle of 7 metres radius; what acceleration pulls it inward?
Take 28 m/s on a 7 m radius and give the centripetal acceleration.
A 6 m/s cart goes round a 0.8 m bend; the track is 2 m wide. Find the centripetal acceleration.
20 m/s on a 4 m radius - what acceleration does the centre supply?
The test rig spins a mass at 22 m/s on a 2 m arm, and the accelerometer reads the inward acceleration; what does it read?
How far away does it come down? A shell leaves at 18 m/s and 55 degrees, with g = 9.81 m/s^2.
A ball is struck off the tee at 28 m/s and climbs away at 35 degrees to the level pitch. With g = 9.8 m/s^2 and no air, the distance to the first bounce is the figure the coach wants.
A launcher fires at 50 m/s at 30 degrees with g = 9.81 m/s^2. The launcher stands 2 m tall. What horizontal range does the projectile get?
The rig fires at 25 m/s, 15 degrees up, with g = 9.8 m/s^2, and the tape measure gives the range; what does it give?
v0 = 36 m/s, theta = 20 degrees, g = 10. Range?
A 7 m/s throw at 40 degrees on a world with g = 10 m/s^2 lands, says a pupil, beyond 5 m. Check it.
A firework shell leaves at 13 m/s angled 50 degrees to the ground, g being 10 m/s^2, and the last thing to find is how far downrange it bursts.
Take 30 m/s at 45 degrees with g = 9.8 m/s^2 and state the horizontal range.
Thrown at 11 metres per second, 65 degrees above the flat, with g = 9.8 m/s^2, how far does the stone travel?
At 60 degrees and 45 m/s, with g = 9.81 m/s^2, the projectile covers what horizontal distance?
